stem: $5,000 is deposited in an account that pays 6% interest compounded annually. What is the balance after 10 years?
eli5: Each year you earn interest on last year's interest too, so the pile grows a little faster every year.

stem: A $20,000 loan is repaid in five equal end-of-year payments at 8% annual interest. What is each payment?
eli5: Each payment covers that year's interest plus a slice of the loan. The capital recovery factor spreads the loan evenly so the last payment clears it exactly.

stem: A plant has fixed costs of $120,000 per year. Each unit costs $18 to make and sells for $30. How many units per year must be sold to break even?
eli5: Every unit sold leaves a little money after paying for itself. Break-even is the number of units whose leftovers add up to the bills you pay no matter what.
solution:
Each unit contributes 30 - 18 = $12 toward fixed costs.

Break-even quantity = \frac{120,000}{12} = 10,000 units.

stem: A project has a 20% chance of losing $50,000, a 50% chance of earning $40,000 and a 30% chance of earning $100,000. What is its expected value?
eli5: Expected value is the average result if you could run the project many times. Weight each outcome by how often it happens and add them up.

stem: A machine has fixed costs of $50,000 per year and variable costs of $12 per unit. What is the average cost per unit at 10,000 units per year?
eli5: Fixed costs are shared out over everything you make. The more you make, the smaller each unit's share.

stem: A task needs 40 hours of direct labor at $35 per hour and $600 of materials. Overhead is charged at 50% of direct labor. What is the total cost?
eli5: Direct costs are the hands and the materials on the job. Overhead is everything in the background, added as a share of the direct cost.

stem: What is the present worth of $10,000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year?
eli5: Money you have to wait for is worth less today, because today's money could have been earning interest the whole time.

stem: A loan charges a nominal rate of 12% per year, compounded monthly. What is the effective annual interest rate?
eli5: Charging 1% twelve times is slightly more than charging 12% once, because each month's interest earns interest too.

stem: A flood wall costs $300,000 to build and $15,000 per year to maintain. It prevents $60,000 of damage per year. Over 20 years at 6%, what is the benefit-cost ratio?
eli5: Put all the good the project does and all it costs into today's dollars, then see how many dollars of good you get per dollar spent.

stem: A machine costs $40,000, costs $3,000 per year to run, and has a salvage value of $5,000 after 8 years. At 10% interest, what is its equivalent uniform annual cost?
eli5: Spread the purchase price over the years like a loan payment, add the yearly running cost, and take off the yearly value of what you get back at the end.

stem: Option A pays a certain $30,000. Option B has a 60% chance of paying $60,000 and a 40% chance of losing $10,000. Based on expected value, which option is better and by how much?
eli5: Compare the sure thing with the average result of the gamble.
